title: Proofreading: Find and Fix Your Errors
summary: A step-by-step proofreading routine for the last minutes of your writing, the most common errors to hunt for, confusing homophones, and two error texts to correct, with full answers.

blocks.text: **Proofreading** means checking your finished writing for errors and correcting them. Many students lose marks not because they do not know the rules, but because they write quickly and never check. A few minutes of careful checking can fix missing capitals, wrong verb forms and comma splices that would otherwise pull your grammar, punctuation and spelling marks down.

blocks.title: Key words
items: **Proofread**: read carefully to find and correct errors.
**Comma splice**: two complete sentences joined only by a comma (I was tired, I went to bed.).
**Run-on sentence**: two or more sentences joined with no punctuation at all.
**Homophones**: words that sound the same but are spelt differently (their / there / they're).

blocks.text: 2. The last five minutes: one check at a time
Keep about five minutes at the end of your writing time to proofread. Read slowly, sentence by sentence, checking one thing at a time:

items: **Sentences**: every sentence complete, with no comma splices or run-ons.
**Verbs**: tense consistent, subject-verb agreement, correct past forms (saw, not seen).
**Punctuation**: capitals, full stops, apostrophes (its/it's), speech marks.
**Spelling**: homophones (their/there/they're, your/you're, where/were) and words you often get wrong.
**Clarity**: pronouns clear, modifiers in the right place, lists parallel.
**Register**: Standard English. Formal or informal to match the task.

blocks.title: How to proofread well
items: Read **slowly**, as if reading aloud in your head. Your eyes skip errors when you read fast.
Point at each word with your pen when checking spelling.
Know **your own** common mistakes (for example, beacuse, missing capitals, alot) and hunt for them first.
Correct neatly: one clean line through the error and the correction above it. Use an insertion mark (^) for a missing word.

rows: Missing capital
on monday we visited cairo tower.
On Monday we visited Cairo Tower.
Comma splice
The road was closed, we took the bridge.
The road was closed, so we took the bridge. / The road was closed. We took the bridge.
Tense shift
She opened the gate and walks inside.
She opened the gate and walked inside.
Agreement
The list of rules are on the wall.
The list of rules is on the wall.
Wrong verb form
I have went there before.
I have been there before.
Apostrophe
The dog wagged it's tail. The boy's played outside.
The dog wagged its tail. The boys played outside.
Homophone
Their going to there aunt's house.
They're going to their aunt's house.
Non-standard form
We should of left earlier.
We should have left earlier.
Missing word
I went the market with my father.
I went to the market with my father.
Dangling modifier
Looking up, a shooting star crossed the sky.
Looking up, I saw a shooting star cross the sky.
Not parallel
I like drawing, to sing and dancing.
I like drawing, singing and dancing.

blocks.text: Proofreading is not usually a separate reading question, but it decides how many marks you keep in **your writing**. The grammar and punctuation part of the writing mark rewards accurate sentences and varied punctuation, and spelling is rewarded separately. Careless errors in simple words are noticed first. In class tests and practice papers, you may also be given a short text with errors to find and correct, like the one below.

blocks.title: المراجعة في آخر خمس دقايق
items: سيب خمس دقايق في الآخر للمراجعة، واقرا ببطء جملة جملة.
دوّر على حاجة واحدة كل مرة: الـ capital والـ full stop، بعدين الأفعال، بعدين الإملاء.
أشهر الأخطاء: its و it's، و their و there، و should of بدل should have، والفاصلة بين جملتين كاملتين.

blocks.text: last weekend me and my cousin visited the national museum, we was amazed by the mummies. Walking through the main hall, the golden mask caught our eyes. The guide told us that the mask has been found in 1922. There was hundreds of visitors, and everyone were taking photos. My cousin wanted to see the jewellery, buying a souvenir and to have lunch. We should of stayed longer, its the best trip I ever had.

items.a: Last weekend, my cousin and I visited the National Museum. We were amazed by the mummies. As we walked through the main hall, the golden mask caught our eyes. The guide told us that the mask had been found in 1922. There were hundreds of visitors, and everyone was taking photos. My cousin wanted to see the jewellery, buy a souvenir and have lunch. We should have stayed longer; it's the best trip I have ever had.

items.q: List the fourteen errors and what was wrong.
items.a: 1. last → Last (capital at the start). 2. me and my cousin → my cousin and I (Standard English subject). 3. national museum → National Museum (name of a place). 4. Comma splice after museum → full stop. 5. we was → we were (agreement). 6. Walking through the main hall, the golden mask... is a dangling modifier → As we walked through the main hall, .... 7. has been found → had been found (backshift in reported speech). 8. There was hundreds → There were hundreds (agreement). 9. everyone were → everyone was (agreement). 10. to see..., buying... and to have → to see..., buy... and have (parallelism). 11. should of → should have. 12. Comma splice after longer → semicolon (or full stop). 13. its → it's (it is). 14. I ever had → I have ever had (present perfect with ever).

blocks.text: Our school have decided to ban mobile phones during lessons. Many students thinks this is unfair, but i agree with the decision. Phones distract students, they also make it harder to concentrate. Last year, my freind lose his phone in class and he cannot focus for the rest of the day. Teachers are not trying to punish us, there trying to help us learn.

items.a: Our school has decided to ban mobile phones during lessons. Many students think this is unfair, but I agree with the decision. Phones distract students. They also make it harder to concentrate. Last year, my friend lost his phone in class and he could not focus for the rest of the day. Teachers are not trying to punish us. They're trying to help us learn.

items.q: List the nine errors in Text 2.
items.a: 1. have decided → has decided (school is singular). 2. students thinks → students think (plural subject). 3. i → I (capital). 4. Comma splice after students → full stop. 5. freind → friend (spelling). 6. lose → lost (past tense: Last year). 7. cannot → could not (keep the past tense). 8. Comma splice after punish us → full stop. 9. there → They're (homophone: they're = they are, with a capital because it now starts a new sentence).

items.q: Correct: Its to hot to play outside today.
items.a: It's too hot to play outside today. (it's = it is, too = more than enough)

items.q: Correct: The childrens toys was all over the floor.
items.a: The children's toys were all over the floor. (children is already plural, add 's. toys is plural, so use were.)

items.q: Correct: I was so tired, I fell asleep on the sofa.
items.a: I was so tired that I fell asleep on the sofa. (or a full stop: I was so tired. I fell asleep on the sofa.)

items.q: Correct: We seen alot of birds at the lake yesterday.
items.a: We saw a lot of birds at the lake yesterday.

items.q: Correct: My sister is taller then me but she don't play basketball.
items.a: My sister is taller than me, but she doesn't play basketball.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Save five minutes. Read slowly. One check at a time: sentences, verbs, punctuation, spelling, clarity, register. Fix neatly.
